data.gender_notes: Fatemah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Fatemah means abundance or plenty. It is also associated with the concept of weaning, signifying detachment from worldly desires. The name Fatemah carries the meaning “Abundance, Plenty, Weaning” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Fatemah usually hope their child will grow to embody abundance, plenty, weaning and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Fatemah is the name of the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), embodying virtues of piety, compassion, and righteousness.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fatemah total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: In the Islamic context, Fatemah is the name of the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) beloved daughter. She is revered as an important figure in Islamic history and is often mentioned in Hadiths (reports of the Prophet's actions, sayings, and teachings). Fatemah is also the name of various other prominent figures in Islamic history, adding to the significance and importance of the name.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, Fatemah represents the concept of detachment from worldly possessions and desires. Named after her in the Quran (Al-An'am, 6:152), she is the embodiment of patience and perseverance. She was the wife of Imam Ali (the fourth Caliph and the prophet's cousin) and is often referred to as Fatemah al-Zahra ("radiant Fatemah"). Fatemah's life, characterized by suffering and loss, is an inspiration for Muslims to remain steadfast in their faith and patience in times of hardship.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Abundance, Plenty, Weaning" symbolizes Fatemah means abundance or plenty. It is also associated with the concept of weaning, signifying detachment from worldly desires.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Fatemah serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of abundance, plenty, weaning.
